recommendations.title: `_purity_findings_with_cache()` in `plan_tool/detail.py` (step 2 "Add the purity-cache persistence module") calls `load_
recommendations.body: `_purity_findings_with_cache()` in `plan_tool/detail.py` (step 2 "Add the purity-cache persistence module") calls `load_purity_cache(cache_path)` with no `valid_step_ids` at both the read-through hit check and the pre-save read-modify-write, even though it has already parsed the plan (`plan = parse_plan(plan_path)`) a few lines above, so `load_purity_cache`'s prune branch never runs in production and entries for steps removed by a split/merge/scope-out accrete unbounded — the exact accretion the plan's "prune orphaned entries on load" requirement exists to stop
recommendations.suggested_action: pass `valid_step_ids={s.id for s in plan.steps}` to the pre-save `load_purity_cache(cache_path)` call in `plan_tool/detail.py:_purity_findings_with_cache()` so every cache write drops orphaned entries

recommendations.body: `_utc_now_iso()` in `plan_tool/purity_cache.py` has no callers — `plan_tool/detail.py:_purity_findings_with_cache()` builds `checked_at` with its own inline `datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")`, duplicating the format literal outside the module that owns the record shape, so a future format change has two sites to touch
recommendations.suggested_action: export the helper as `utc_now_iso()` in `plan_tool/purity_cache.py` and call it for `checked_at` in `plan_tool/detail.py:_purity_findings_with_cache()`
